1. (Currently Amended) A golf tee comprising a long lasting combination of a golf tee and a force absorbing member in association therewith, said tee including a ground insertion end, a ball support end and a shaft in between, said member surrounding said shaft and being located below said ball support end and having an outer diameter less than that of a golf ball but large enough and located so as to protect said support end from impact from a golf club strike after a golf ball has been struck from said tee, wherein __said force absorbing member is permanently affixed to said shaft__.

2. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 1, wherein said tee is formed from a material that enables the shaft to withstand damage from a strike on the resilient member __and wherein said force absorbing member is formed from a material having a durometer hardness greater than 90__.

3. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 1, wherein said tee is formed from a member selected from the group consisting of wood, plastic and metal, __and wherein said force absorbing member comprises a composite material formed from multiple layers of different elastomeric materials__.

4. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 3, wherein said tee is formed from a hardwood __and wherein said force absorbing member is bonded to said shaft through a mechanical interlocking structure__.

5. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 3, wherein said tee is formed from an engineering plastic __and wherein said force absorbing member is vulcanized to said shaft__.

6. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 5, wherein said tee is formed from a polycarbonate __and wherein said force absorbing member is chemically bonded to said shaft__.

7. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 3, wherein said tee is formed from nylon __and wherein said force absorbing member comprises a laminated elastomer structure__.

8. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 3, wherein said tee is formed from a malleable metal __and wherein said force absorbing member is press-fitted onto said shaft with an interference fit__.

9. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 8, wherein said tee is formed from aluminum __and wherein said force absorbing member is secured to said shaft through a threaded connection__.

10. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 9, wherein said force absorbing member is formed from a force absorbing material comprising a natural or man-made material __having a durometer hardness of at least 60__.

11. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 1, wherein said force absorbing member is formed from a force absorbing material comprising a natural or man-made material __that is permanently bonded to said shaft and has a durometer hardness greater than 90__.

12. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 11, wherein said force absorbing material has a hardness of from about 30 to about 90 durometer __and comprises a multi-layer composite structure__.

13. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 12, wherein said force absorbing material comprises a neoprene having a hardness of from about 50 to about 60 durometer __and is chemically cross-linked to the shaft material__.

14. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 11, wherein said force absorbing material comprises a neoprene __and is permanently affixed to said shaft through vulcanization__.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 15, wherein the tee is formed from a material that enables the shaft to withstand damage from a strike on the resilient member __and wherein said force absorbing member is formed from a material having a durometer hardness greater than 90__.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 15, wherein the tee is formed from a member selected from the group consisting of wood, plastic and metal, __and wherein said force absorbing member comprises a composite material formed from multiple layers of different elastomeric materials__.

18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17, wherein the tee is formed from a hardwood __and wherein said force absorbing member is bonded to said shaft through a mechanical interlocking structure__.

19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17, wherein the tee is formed from an engineering plastic __and wherein said force absorbing member is vulcanized to said shaft__.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 19, wherein the tee is formed from a polycarbonate __and wherein said force absorbing member is chemically bonded to said shaft__.

21. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17, wherein the tee is formed from nylon __and wherein said force absorbing member comprises a laminated elastomer structure__.

22. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17, wherein the tee is formed from a malleable metal __and wherein said force absorbing member is press-fitted onto said shaft with an interference fit__.

23. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 22, wherein the tee is formed from aluminum __and wherein said force absorbing member is secured to said shaft through a threaded connection__.

24. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 23, wherein the force absorbing member is formed from a force absorbing material comprising a natural or man-made material __having a durometer hardness of at least 60__.

25. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 15, wherein the force absorbing member is formed from a force absorbing material comprising a natural or man-made material __that is permanently bonded to said shaft and has a durometer hardness greater than 90__.
